idFamilies.JAVA-XNA: A gap between CNA-Java and the original XNA 4.0 contract.
idFamilies.JAVA-NATIVE: A gap at the CNA C ABI boundary: a route, a shape or a verification.
idFamilies.JAVA-EXT: A CNA capability outside XNA 4.0, belonging under org.openeggbert.cna.extensions.
idFamilies.JAVA-TEMPLATE: Work in the sibling cna-java-template consumer canary.
idFamilies.JAVA-UPSTREAM: Blocked on cnanext or sharp-runtimenext. Never worked around in Java.

tasks.title: Qualify against the live cnanext built on sharp-runtimenext
tasks.currentState: Qualified against an unrelated historical CNA checkout and a pinned /tmp artifact at ABI 0.7.0.
tasks.expectedState: libcna_c_api built out of tree from cnanext against sharp-runtimenext, HEADLESS/HEADLESS/NULL, and every native check run against it.

tasks.title: Migrate the ABI gate from 0.7.0 to the live 0.20.0 policy
tasks.currentState: A hardcoded exact-minor check against 0.7 with no stated policy.
tasks.expectedState: The required version comes from the manifest; major and minor are exact, patch is free, and each rule has a negative-mutation test.

tasks.title: Make a stale JNI declaration a compile error
tasks.currentState: 426 hand-written function-pointer typedefs that dlsym could never check.
tasks.expectedState: Every dispatch-table slot declared CNA_JNI_ROUTE(symbol), whose type is the header's own declaration.

tasks.title: Generate the mechanical half of the native boundary
tasks.currentState: Every route hand-written, which is where drift came from.
tasks.expectedState: tools/native-abi/generate_jni.py derives JNI, dispatch slots, LOAD lines and Java declarations from the headers; generateJniCheck fails on stale output.

tasks.title: Explain every canonical CNA C API function
tasks.currentState: 723 bound routes and 3,328 unexplained ones.
tasks.expectedState: Every one of the 4,051 canonical functions classified, with zero UNMAPPED_REQUIRES_REVIEW, and the public surface that reaches each bound route derived from the JNI call graph and the Java sources.

tasks.title: Inventory the complete XNA 4.0 reference corpus
tasks.authority: the original Microsoft assemblies at xna4-decomp/dlls, SHA-256 pinned
tasks.currentState: One seven-assembly Windows runtime profile.
tasks.expectedState: A ten-assembly full runtime superset profile and a separate seven-assembly Content Pipeline build-time profile, both hash-pinned, with the selected profile kept as a subset regression gate.

tasks.title: Keep XNA's Dispose() name and add close() as the Java bridge
tasks.authority: 36 CLR types declaring a public parameterless Dispose
tasks.currentState: Dispose() renamed to close(), the one place a legal XNA name was dropped for Java convention.
tasks.expectedState: Dispose() keeps its name with the CLR member's modifiers; close() delegates to it so every disposable type is still an AutoCloseable.
tasks.compatibility: Additive. 33 types gained Dispose(); no member was removed and every close() call site still compiles.

tasks.title: Project the GamerServices and Avatar families
tasks.currentState: Only GamerServicesComponent existed; 51 types were missing from the full profile.
tasks.expectedState: The whole namespace projected and backed by CNA's gamer-services routes.

tasks.title: Project Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Net
tasks.currentState: The whole namespace was missing; 23 types.
tasks.expectedState: Sessions, discovery, rosters, machines, packets and the nine session events projected, session and gamer state backed by CNA.

tasks.title: Raise the nine NetworkSession events and the two SignedInGamer events from CNA
tasks.currentState: The event members exist and accept listeners; no native producer raises them, because their CNA routes take a real callback the generator refuses.
tasks.expectedState: Hand-written JNI callback plumbing that attaches the JVM thread, contains a Java exception, and survives session teardown, so each event has a real producer.
tasks.blocker: None. It needs the callback lifetime work that the media and storage families already have, applied to eleven more callbacks.
tests: a native event test per event, plus a teardown stress

tasks.title: Inventory the Content Pipeline build-time profile
tasks.authority: the seven Content Pipeline assemblies, SHA-256 pinned in xna40-content-pipeline.json
tasks.currentState: The profile exists and is pinned; nothing is measured against it yet.
tasks.expectedState: A measured gap report, and a decision recorded on whether a Java content pipeline belongs in this binding at all.

tasks.title: Expose CNA's extended graphics layer
tasks.currentState: 1,733 routes classified CNA_EXTENSION_CANDIDATE; none reachable from Java.
tasks.expectedState: A typed Java facade for the canonical concepts, with truthful availability queries and NOT_SUPPORTED preserved rather than downgraded.

tasks.title: Expose CNA's runtime and device extensions
tasks.authority: core_ext.h, devices.h, sensors.h, input_haptics.h, input_joystick.h, input_text.h, input_cursor.h, input_devices.h
tasks.currentState: Classified as extension candidates; none reachable from Java.
tasks.expectedState: Typed Java facades under the extension namespace, never inside Microsoft.Xna.Framework.

tasks.title: Expose the .cnb content format
tasks.currentState: 272 routes, none bound.
tasks.expectedState: A Java facade over the container, its schemas and its loader registry.

tasks.title: Use the whole-buffer vertex upload route
tasks.currentState: The route is loaded, so the library must export it, but no JNI entry point reaches it: SetData always takes the windowed form.
tasks.expectedState: Either the whole-buffer form is used for a whole-buffer upload, or the route is dropped from the manifest.

tasks.title: Bind the native Model routes behind the managed XNB model graph
tasks.currentState: 127 routes deferred; Load<Model> is managed-only.
tasks.expectedState: Model, ModelMesh, ModelMeshPart and ModelBone reach CNA, and the skinned, morph and animation routes move to the extension namespace.

tasks.title: Bind the remaining input routes
tasks.currentState: 132 routes deferred: gamepad capabilities and vibration, keyboard scancodes, mouse capture, touch panel details.
tasks.expectedState: The XNA-shaped ones bound; the rest reclassified as extension candidates.

tasks.title: Add a truthful modern-CNA canary to the template
tasks.currentState: The template exercises the XNA surface only.
tasks.expectedState: An opt-in extensions smoke that proves the Java extension facade compiles externally, the JNI route exists, the availability query is truthful, and HEADLESS NOT_SUPPORTED is represented as itself.

tasks.title: Native StorageContainer path containment
tasks.currentState: Java enforces XNA's containment before the JNI call; CNA itself accepts parent traversal.
tasks.expectedState: CNA refuses a path that escapes the container, so the guarantee can be credited to the runtime rather than to the binding.
tasks.blocker: cnanext storage: cna_storage_container_* accept a path containing parent traversal.

tasks.title: Project CNA's CRT and depth-reduction post-process effects
tasks.currentState: Not bound. Both routes produce a CNA_EffectHandle, and the Java Effect's adopting constructors are package-private, so a Java facade needs a reviewed cross-package accessor of the kind FacadeFactory already uses for Texture2D and GraphicsDevice.
tasks.expectedState: CrtEffect and DepthEffect projected as extension types that are real XNA Effects, so SpriteBatch.Begin can take them.
tasks.blocker: None upstream. It needs the facade accessor, not a CNA change.
tests: an extension test that creates each effect and round-trips its parameters
